video.title: The Most Passive $104K/M Online Business You've Never Heard Of

summary: Kyle explains his website landlord model: build and rank a basic local service website, then rent its calls and form leads to a local business for a monthly fee. He says the work is concentrated in choosing niches, building sites and finding the first client; once a site ranks and a client is in place, it can require little ongoing attention. Chris also describes an unmonetized pet and horse cremation lead site that receives inquiries. The discussion emphasizes low competition, proving lead quality with a free trial and favoring simple, predictable pricing over maximizing each site's revenue.

speakers.name: Kyle
speakers.description: Surname not stated; runs a website landlord business.

ideas.name: Local website landlord / rank-and-rent lead generation
ideas.one_liner: Build a local service website, rank it in Google, and rent its tracked calls and form leads to a local business.
ideas.business_model: Primarily a negotiated flat monthly fee for local leads; Kyle also describes a trusted-client commission arrangement and an initial one-off payment.
ideas.customer: Local service businesses, including junk removal, auto glass, concrete, spray foam insulation, epoxy flooring, attorneys and other home-service providers.
ideas.problem: Small local businesses need high-intent customer leads but may not want to risk a large fixed marketing contract without proof of results.
ideas.offer: Build a generic niche-and-city website, rank it through local SEO, then forward tracked phone calls and form leads to a local business. Offer an initial free trial so the business can judge lead quality.

pricing.model: Usually a negotiated, flat monthly fee. Kyle describes historical client-specific deals, an initial upfront payment, and a commission exception for a trusted contractor.

price_points.label: Initial payment from first attorney client
Early monthly fee for first attorney client
Later monthly fee as lead flow grew for first attorney client
Later base SEO fee for first attorney client
Additional fee for a new client signed by the attorney
Host's hypothetical pay-per-call price, not Kyle's preferred model

pricing.notes: Kyle says he prefers predictable flat fees and has stopped using tiered call pricing because it creates invoice disputes. The first attorney deal later changed structure; these are historical examples, not a single current rate card.

acquisition_channels.details: Rank a generic niche-and-city site for local search terms to attract people actively looking for the service.

quote.text: I get that website ranking to page one and once it's on page one of Google so that it shows up anytime somebody searches for junk removal services in Austin, Texas, obviously people are going to be clicking on it.
quote.speaker: Kyle

acquisition_channels.details: After the site has calls, find local providers through Google, Yelp and Yellow Pages, make a list in Excel and call businesses with an offer of a free trial.

quote.text: I just literally go to Google, Yelp, yellow pages and make a list on a, on an Excel sheet of all the businesses in town that offer that service.
quote.speaker: Kyle

acquisition_channels.details: For his first sale, Kyle contacted an old high-school friend who was an attorney; he also advises starting with one's network.

quote.text: I made a screencast video where I recorded my screen and showed him how this business model works and how I could build a Macite targeting Torrance.
quote.speaker: Kyle

ideas.delivery: Create a generic website for a service in a specific city, improve its ranking with content and backlinks, and place a tracking phone number on it. The number forwards calls to the paying provider; the tracking platform can send call recordings and caller details to the client. The site can also collect form leads. Kyle says low-competition sites often need little maintenance after ranking, though building, SEO and replacing clients still require work.
unit_economics_claims: Kyle claims basic site overhead can be about USD 25 per month per site.
Kyle reports company revenue around USD 100,000 per month and overhead below USD 5,000 per month; elsewhere he says he personally makes around USD 35,000 per month.
Kyle says his first client paid USD 6,000 upfront, and later describes several changing monthly fee arrangements.
Kyle gives an example of an auto glass site producing about 50 calls per month for a USD 600 monthly fee.
Kyle says one to three free trials typically produce a locked-in business owner.
Kyle says clients who stay beyond six months may remain for about five years or more.
Kyle reports an exception where a trusted concrete contractor pays 10% commission.
ideas.startup_cost: Kyle says site overhead can be about USD 25 per month for hosting, domain and tracking phone number. Initial build and learning costs are not stated; the first client paid USD 6,000 upfront.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Kyle says his first win came after three months. He contacted a former school friend and received an initial USD 6,000 payment.

acquisition.how: Organic search can bring in leads with limited ongoing work after ranking, but site selection and SEO require work and the paying clients are found through manual calls. UK cold calling needs appropriate screening, including TPS/CTPS checks.

onboarding.how: A human negotiates and sets up the free trial, client contact details and call routing; the tracking platform can automate forwarding and notifications.

delivery.how: Call forwarding, form capture and recording can run automatically. Site building, content, backlinks and occasional ranking checks need human work; Kyle says some low-competition sites need little later attention.

billing.how: Recurring flat fees can be billed automatically, but Kyle says he manually follows up on failed cards and late payments.

support.how: Many clients reportedly need little contact after setup, but disputes, payment failures and client replacement require human follow-up.

uk_applicability.notes: Local SEO and renting lead flow to UK service businesses can work on the same basic model. The specific cities, niches, prices and search competition need UK research, and the manual cold-call step needs UK screening and privacy compliance.

risks: Google ranking changes or stronger competitors can reduce the site's lead flow.
The model depends on targeting low-competition niches; Kyle warns against entering heavily funded markets such as personal injury in Los Angeles.
A client may fail to answer calls or follow up promptly, wasting leads and weakening retention.
Without job tracking, commission or pay-per-call billing can create disputes and depends on trust.
Flat fees without contracts can make clients easy to lose; the operator needs a replacement prospect pipeline.
Late or failed client payments require follow-up.
In the UK, cold calling needs appropriate TPS/CTPS screening, and handling call recordings and lead data requires care.

tactics.name: Choose a low-competition niche and city
steps: Look for a local service and city where search demand exists but competing sites are weak.
Avoid heavily funded national or major-city SEO markets.
Compare the supply of providers with the apparent demand for the service.
Consider adjacent services and cities as separate opportunities.

warnings.warning: Kyle says SEO sites should target low-competition local terms; he advises against competing against heavily funded national or major-city sites.
A site can generate leads that are not valuable to a buyer if local providers lack capacity or do not serve the relevant area.
Calls can be missed or followed up slowly; Kyle says call recordings help show whether leads arrived and how they were handled.
Commission and pay-per-call deals require reliable lead and job tracking; Kyle says he avoids them when he cannot verify closed work.
Tiered call pricing can lead clients to dispute invoices and audit individual leads, so Kyle prefers a predictable flat fee.
Kyle says some clients' cards fail and one or two clients may not pay in a month, requiring follow-up.
Kyle says the course and community he purchased no longer exist; he also advises vetting a course before spending heavily.
Kyle says the website landlord's client-acquisition step involves manual cold calls. In the UK, screen business cold calls against TPS/CTPS and follow applicable PECR and data-protection rules.
The host promotes GoHighLevel and the TKO Owners community; Kyle promotes Rent Local Sites and his TikTok account. These are promotional interests, separate from the business examples.

lessons.lesson: Prove that a business can deliver before asking a client to commit; a free trial of tracked leads lowers the buyer's perceived risk.
Start with warm contacts when possible. A trusted first customer can create urgency to deliver and provide a case study for later sales.
A strong, specific offer makes sales calls easier: describe the service, location and existing lead flow, then offer a low-risk trial.
Choose lower-competition local search terms where a basic site can beat neglected competitors, rather than chasing the largest search markets.
Use call tracking and recordings to make lead delivery visible and reduce disagreements about which calls came from the site.
Predictable flat pricing can be more valuable than maximizing short-term revenue if it reduces disputes and keeps clients for longer.
Keep operations simple. Kyle says a basic spreadsheet and a small software stack can be enough for managing clients and sites.
For a local service site, clarity and speed can matter more than polished design; the site should make its service and location obvious.
Automating a business does not remove the initial work: the site still has to be researched, built, ranked and matched to a client.
A lifestyle business can be a deliberate goal. The speakers value time freedom and sustainable income over pursuing the largest possible exit.
When selling leads on commission, use reliable tracking and work only with partners you trust; otherwise the operator cannot verify closed jobs.

evidence_quality.rationale: Kyle describes a first-hand business, concrete workflows, named tools and several specific revenue, cost, pricing and retention figures. The figures are self-reported and not independently verified; the introduction's USD 104,000 monthly figure differs from Kyle's later USD 35,000 personal monthly figure and roughly USD 100,000 company monthly figure.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The host reads a GoHighLevel promotion and promotes TKO Owners. Kyle directs viewers to Rent Local Sites and his TikTok account. The course Kyle bought is said to no longer exist.
